answer: The Ephemeral Zenith Protocol assigns each agent a registration window timed to a random orbital comet trajectory. At the zenith of this pass, the network broadcasts a high-entropy, state-dependent opal challenge. The agent must solve and cryptographically bind its genesis key to this exact temporal node within milliseconds. Because the challenge permanently alters local state and never repeats, an attacker cannot replay past successes or parallelize creation; spawning a Sybil requires capturing a unique, fleeting microsecond of global entropy at immense computational and latency cost.
